subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Proportional Control: The P in PID
description: A quick win: understand Proportional Control: The P in PID.

hook.text: Big error? Big correction. Small error? Small correction. That's proportional control.

buildup.text: The output is simply the error multiplied by a gain constant Kp. Higher Kp means stronger response.

discovery.text: Too much gain and the system overshoots and oscillates. Too little and it responds sluggishly.

twist.text: Proportional control alone leaves a steady-state error — the output settles close to but not exactly at the setpoint.

climax.text: Simple proportional controllers run basic motor speed regulation and simple heating systems.

punchline.text: Multiply the error by a gain — proportional control is intuitive but imperfect.

quiz.question: What limitation does proportional-only control typically have?
options: It cannot respond to changes in setpoint
It leaves a steady-state error — the output never quite reaches the setpoint
It always causes the system to become unstable
